_about: Hand-kept input of scripts/ontology/census.js (ONT-000). kinds: id → the person's sentence, the question the kind asks before any schema, what tells it from its neighbours, what it projects to. classification: row id (source|from.field, or source|*.field for every collection's field of that name) → kind, for the in-repo sources only; the private rows are classified in the private folder. notes: the three notes attributed to kinds. depthSentences: the deepest path per source in words. oral: Richard's list. A kind is added here only after a row was read off an app; the script refuses one with no row.

belongs-to.question: Must every one have one, or can it stand alone? Can it move to another later? When the one it belongs to goes, does this go with it, stay orphaned, or block the removal?
belongs-to.distinguishes: one target, no details on the link itself; read the other way it is 'has many' (the same edge)
belongs-to.projectsTo: Link (Pointer) with required/optional and an on-delete rule; the reverse read is a query, not a column

is-on.sentence: a {from} is on a {to} for a while, with details of its own
is-on.question: Can it be on two at once? Does it start and end (dates, active)? What stays and what goes when it ends? Which details belong to the link and not to either end (a role, a type, a position)?
is-on.distinguishes: a junction record that carries details; a plain pairing with none is 'together'
is-on.projectsTo: a collection of its own with two Links and the details as fields; never a Links (Relation) column, which cannot hold a date

together.question: Does the pairing ever need a date, a reason, a role or an order? (Then it is 'is-on'.) Can the same pair be listed twice?
together.projectsTo: Links (Relation) or a junction collection; the unique pair rule

one-of.sentence: a {from}'s {field} is one of a fixed list
one-of.question: Who may add to the list, and does adding need a developer? Is the list the same for everyone? Does a value ever retire (then it is a lifecycle, not a choice)? Will you ever need details about a list entry (then it is a collection)?
one-of.distinguishes: a value from a declared list on the record itself, not a link to a record
one-of.projectsTo: Choice (String + oneOf rule); the mutant is free text where a list belongs

many-by-list.sentence: a {from} carries a list of {to} on itself
many-by-list.question: Will you ever ask it the other way round ('which {from}s name this one')? Will the list need details per entry? If either, each entry is its own link.
many-by-list.distinguishes: ids or values stored as an array column, no record per entry
many-by-list.projectsTo: List (Array); the mutant is a list of ids that nobody can query from the other side

part-of-tree.question: How deep can it go? Can a thing be moved under another? Can it be its own ancestor? Does a child inherit anything from its parent?
part-of-tree.distinguishes: a link from a collection to itself
part-of-tree.projectsTo: a Link to the same collection; the path operation walks it (ONT-004)

exists-elsewhere.sentence: a {from} also exists in another system, known there by its own id
exists-elsewhere.question: Can it exist here before it exists there, or there before here — and what is silently skipped when it does? Which side wins when they disagree? What is it called over there? What happens over there when it ends here?
exists-elsewhere.distinguishes: an id or a provenance record naming another system, not a record in this one
exists-elsewhere.projectsTo: a Text field per system, unique, plus a sync log; the enrolment note is this kind's unasked question

same-as.sentence: two {from}s turned out to be one thing
same-as.question: How do you tell? Who decides when the system is not sure? Which record survives and which fields win? Can a merge be undone?
same-as.distinguishes: a link between records of the same collection that means identity, not hierarchy
same-as.projectsTo: a 'superseded by' Link on the same collection plus a match record; never a delete

ends.sentence: a {from} can end without being deleted
ends.question: When it ends, what stays and what goes — its record, its history, the things on it, its access elsewhere, the lists it is on? Can it come back, and does coming back make a new one or revive the old? Who may end it?
ends.distinguishes: a status, an active flag, an end date, an archive or erasure record — the record is kept
ends.projectsTo: a status Choice or a Date, a rule for each linked thing, and a 'delete: nobody' permission; the archive note is this kind's unasked question

happened-to.sentence: something happened to a {from} at a time, and the record of it is kept
happened-to.question: Is it kept forever? Can it be undone, and does undoing make a new record or remove this one? Who did it, and who may see the history? Does the thing it happened to need it to exist?
happened-to.distinguishes: a record that is an event about another record (a log, an action, an attendance, a submission, a read receipt)
happened-to.projectsTo: a collection with a Link, a Date and a 'who' Link; update and delete: nobody

owned-by.sentence: a {from} is seen and changed by whoever it belongs to, and by nobody else unless said
owned-by.question: Who else may see it — a role, an admin of the thing it sits on, everyone? Does ownership follow a path (the holder of the account the person is on)? What happens to it when its owner ends?
owned-by.distinguishes: a rule about visibility, not a fact about the world: creator-owns, an access list, a tenant, an admin link
owned-by.projectsTo: the security file's permissions and creatorOwns; a path-shaped rule needs ONT-004

extends.sentence: a {from} is extra detail about one {to}, at most one each
extends.question: Is there ever more than one? Does it exist without the thing it extends? Is it computed (then nobody edits it) or written by a person?
extends.distinguishes: a one-to-one link, usually unique or the record's own key
extends.projectsTo: a Link with a unique rule; or fields on the thing itself when it is small

by-name.sentence: a {from} names its {to} by something a person could retype (an email, a code)
by-name.question: What if it is misspelled, or changes, or two things share it? Should it be a link instead?
by-name.distinguishes: a natural key stored as text where a Link would be
by-name.projectsTo: a Link; the mutant is the text itself

points-at-one-of.sentence: a {from} points at one thing that may be any of several kinds, and says which
points-at-one-of.question: Which kinds can it point at, exactly? What happens when the thing it points at goes? Can it be re-pointed?
points-at-one-of.distinguishes: an id beside a kind field; no single target collection
points-at-one-of.projectsTo: a kind Choice plus a Text id; the mutant is an id with no kind beside it

notes.note: the archive note (what stays, what ends when a person is archived)
notes.question: When a person stops, what stays and what goes — their record and its history, the account they are on, their access to the things elsewhere, the lists they are on? Can they come back, and is that the old record revived or a new one?

notes.note: the enrolment note (enrolment elsewhere silently skipped)
notes.question: Can a person be added here before they exist over there — and if they can, what is silently skipped, and how would anyone notice?

notes.note: the incident report (a paying member invisible for an unknown period; the remediation that made a person without the links)
notes.question: What must be linked for a thing to count as what you call it — is a person with no link to an account a member, or just a contact? When something arrives from elsewhere, which links must be made for it to count?

depthSentences.acme: the company each person who attended a session works for (attendance → the attendee row → the person → their employment → the company); the account-holder rule, used eight times, is four hops (person-on-account → account → company → its admins → the person asking)
depthSentences.template:members-area: the members of one association, by the person signed in
depthSentences.tirion: for each person: the editions they registered for, how many sessions they attended and what they paid (registration → edition, attendance, transaction, joined per person)
depthSentences.sentinel: the portfolio a question's segment family belongs to

oral.status: not yet taken down — ONT-000 step 5 needs Richard in conversation
